findings.hypothesis: Requests placed through the online delivery channel account for almost the entire drop from "requested a consultation" to "paid and confirmed": 173,053 online requests converted at 50.19% (86,850), leaving ~86,203 unconfirmed — nearly the full top gap of 87,511. This plausibly happens because online routing, matching timeouts or client-side failures produce many "abandoned by system" events before payment/confirmation.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab the "abandoned by system" events and payment-failure/error logs by delivery_channel; run a short A/B where a repair/fallback routing is applied to a random subset of online traffic and measure lift in conversion to "paid and confirmed".

segments: customers paying in cash (how they pay = cash)
findings.hypothesis: Customers choosing cash represent a very large and low-converting group: 154,950 cash entries but only 72,093 reached "paid and confirmed" (46.53%), a loss of 82,857 — which itself explains the majority of the overall gap. Likely causes are payment-path friction, a failing cash checkout flow, or a UX that pushes cash users to abandon before confirmation.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab payer x delivery_channel to see overlap with online; instrument detailed payment-step logging for cash users to capture failure/error codes; run an A/B where cash users see a simplified 'one-tap confirm' flow and measure conversion to "paid and confirmed".

findings.hypothesis: Web sessions convert far worse than native apps: 18,101 web requests but only 6,443 reached "paid and confirmed" (35.59%). This suggests a web-specific technical or UX failure in the payment/confirmation flow (for example broken deep links, payment iframe problems, or client-side JS errors) that causes system abandons.
findings.confirm_via: Segment web sessions by error logs and payment-step completion, and run an A/B test: improved web checkout (or a prompt to open the native app) vs current flow; measure conversion to "paid and confirmed."

findings.hypothesis: Booked-ahead (scheduled) requests convert worse (42.28%) than walk-in requests (62.79%) even though scheduled has far fewer entries. This could reflect doctor-side rejections, scheduling timeouts, or user cancellations during the waiting period for a scheduled slot.
findings.confirm_via: Cross-tab scheduled requests with cancellation/rejection reasons (e.g., rejected_by_doctor, ingin berkonsultasi dengan dokter lain) and run a small experiment adding confirmations or a pre-hold for scheduled slots to see if scheduled->paid-and-confirmed conversion improves.

findings.hypothesis: Two late-evening hours show materially lower conversion (22: 45.05% of 11,367; 21: 52.31% of 13,847). This is consistent with doctor availability/timeout effects or capacity bottlenecks at those hours producing more "abandoned by system" or long wait complaints.
findings.confirm_via: Compare doctor online capacity and match latency by hour_of_day; run targeted capacity/priority-matching experiments during hours 21–22 and measure conversion uplift to "paid and confirmed."

findings.stage: doctor joined the chat -> consultation completed
findings.hypothesis: Once a consultation reaches the "doctor joined the chat" stage, it almost always completes (99.97% of 133,592), so the main failure window is before the doctor joins / before payment and confirmation.
findings.confirm_via: No further confirm needed to act: prioritize diagnostics and fixes on the path from "requested a consultation" to "paid and confirmed" (routing, payment, and platform stability).

growth_ideas.title: One-tap cash checkout
growth_ideas.rationale: A simplified, single-action cash confirmation will reduce dropout at the payment/confirmation step where cash users currently convert at 46.53%.
growth_ideas.description: When a user selects cash, surface a single confirmation button that creates a backend 'pending cash' booking and immediately marks the consultation as confirmed in-app; reconcile payments asynchronously and surface clear status. A/B test against the current multi-step cash flow.

growth_ideas.title: Web-to-app deep-link prompt
growth_ideas.rationale: Web traffic converts far worse (35.59%); nudging web users to the native app or offering an improved web checkout should recover a measurable portion of that loss.
growth_ideas.description: Detect web sessions entering the checkout and show a prominent banner offering to 'Open in Halodoc app' (deep link) plus an A/B test of an improved single-page web checkout flow; measure conversion to "paid and confirmed."

growth_ideas.title: Peak-hour priority matching
growth_ideas.rationale: Conversion drops in late-evening hours; increasing matching priority or temporary capacity in those hours should reduce timeouts and system abandons.
growth_ideas.description: Implement a peak-hour routing rule that prioritizes available doctors for requests between 20:00–23:00 (or auto-enables overflow doctors), plus a small trial that boxes a % of traffic into the new routing and measures lift to "paid and confirmed."

growth_ideas.title: Scheduled pre‑hold and confirmation
growth_ideas.rationale: Scheduled bookings convert worse than walk-ins; a lightweight pre-hold or pre-confirmation step should reduce cancellations and doctor rejections for scheduled slots.
growth_ideas.description: For scheduled requests, place a short 'slot hold' and send automated confirmation prompts with an easy reschedule/backup-doctor option; measure whether scheduled->paid-and-confirmed conversion rises versus control.
